column1: An accident that occurred in the skies over the Grand Canyon in 1956 resulted in the establishment of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to regulate and oversee the operation of aircraft in the skies over the United States, which were becoming quite congested.
column2: 1956年，大峡谷上空发生的一起事故促成了美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）的成立。该机构负责规范和监督航空器在美国上空的运行，当时这片空域正变得相当拥挤。
column8: Federal Aviation Administration|n. 美国联邦航空管理局

column1: The resulting structure of air traffic control has greatly increased the safety of flight in the United States, and similar air traffic control procedures are also in place over much of the rest of the world.
column2: 由此建立的空中交通管制体系大大提高了美国的飞行安全水平。世界其他许多地区的空域也采用了类似的管制程序。
column3: resulting structure|n. 由此建立的体系
column4: air traffic control|n. 空中交通管制
column6: safety of flight|n. 飞行安全
column10: over much of|在……的大部分地区上空

column1: Rudimentary air traffic control (ATC) existed well before the Grand Canyon disaster.
column2: 早在大峡谷空难之前，就已经有了初步的空中交通管制。
column3: Rudimentary|adj. 初步的，尚不完善的
column4: air traffic control|n. 空中交通管制

column1: As early as the 1920s, the earliest air traffic controllers manually guided aircraft in the vicinity of the airports, using lights and flags, while beacons and flashing lights were placed along cross-country routes to establish the earliest airways.
column2: 早在20世纪20年代，第一批空中交通管制员就用灯光和旗帜，以人工方式引导机场附近的飞机。与此同时，人们沿国内长途飞行路线设置信标和闪光灯，建起了最早的空中航路。
column4: air traffic controllers|n. 空中交通管制员
column12: cross-country routes|横跨国内的长途飞行路线

column1: However, this purely visual system was useless in bad weather, and, by the 1930s, radio communication was coming into use for ATC.
column2: 不过，这套完全依赖目视的系统在恶劣天气下毫无用处。到了20世纪30年代，无线电通信开始用于空中交通管制。

column1: The first region to have something approximating today’s ATC was New York City, with other major metropolitan areas following soon after.
column2: 纽约市最先建立了与今天的空管体系相近的系统，其他主要大都市地区很快也跟了上来。
column5: major metropolitan areas|n. 主要大都市地区
column6: following soon after|不久后相继跟进

column1: In the 1940s, ATC centres could and did take advantage of the newly developed radar and improved radio communication brought about by the Second World War, but the system remained rudimentary.
column2: 20世纪40年代，空管中心已经能够利用二战催生的新型雷达和改进后的无线电通信技术，而且确实这样做了。不过，空管系统仍很初步。
column3: could and did|能够且确实这样做了

column1: It was only after the creation of the FAA that full-scale regulation of America’s airspace took place, and this was fortuitous, for the advent of the jet engine suddenly resulted in a large number of very fast planes, reducing pilots’ margin of error and practically demanding some set of rules to keep everyone well separated and operating safely in the air.
column2: 直到美国联邦航空管理局成立之后，美国才开始对本国空域实施全面管制。这个时机恰好合适，因为喷气发动机的问世一下子带来了大批飞行速度极快的飞机，使飞行员出错的余地变小，几乎非得订出一套规则，让各架飞机保持足够的间隔，在空中安全飞行。

column1: Many people think that ATC consists of a row of controllers sitting in front of their radar screens at the nation’s airports, telling arriving and departing traffic what to do.
column2: 许多人以为，空中交通管制就是全国各地机场里一排排管制员坐在雷达屏幕前，指挥进场和离场的飞机。
column7: arriving and departing traffic|n. 进场与离场的飞机

column1: This is a very incomplete part of the picture.
column2: 这只说到了空中交通管制的很小一部分。
column4: part of the picture|整体情况的一个方面

column1: The FAA realised that the airspace over the United States would at any time have many different kinds of planes, flying for many different purposes, in a variety of weather conditions, and the same kind of structure was needed to accommodate all of them.
column2: 美国联邦航空管理局意识到，在任何时候，美国上空都会有多种飞机，它们的飞行目的各不相同，遇到的天气条件也各不相同，因此需要一套统一的空域管理体系，兼顾所有这些情况。

column1: To meet this challenge, the following elements were put into effect.
column2: 为应对这一挑战，以下措施得以实施。
column3: meet this challenge|应对这一挑战
column4: following elements|n. 下列几项措施

column1: First, ATC extends over virtually the entire United States.
column2: 首先，空中交通管制几乎覆盖美国全境。

column1: In general, from 365m above the ground and higher, the entire country is blanketed by controlled airspace.
column2: 一般来说，全国离地365米及以上的空域都属于管制空域。

column1: In certain areas, mainly near airports, controlled airspace extends down to 215m above the ground, and, in the immediate vicinity of an airport, all the way down to the surface.
column2: 在某些地区，主要是机场附近，管制空域的下限降至距地面215米。在紧邻机场的地方，管制空域一直延伸到地面。
column9: all the way down to|一直向下延伸至

column1: Controlled airspace is that airspace in which FAA regulations apply.
column2: 管制空域就是适用联邦航空管理局相关规定的空域。

column1: Elsewhere, in uncontrolled airspace, pilots are bound by fewer regulations.
column2: 在其他地方，也就是非管制空域内，飞行员须遵守的规章较少。

column1: In this way, the recreational pilot who simply wishes to go flying for a while without all the restrictions imposed by the FAA has only to stay in uncontrolled airspace, below 365m, while the pilot who does want the protection afforded by ATC can easily enter the controlled airspace.
column2: 这样，休闲飞行员如果只想飞上一会儿，不想受联邦航空管理局种种限制的约束，只需留在365米以下的非管制空域。而希望得到空中交通管制保护的飞行员，则可很方便地进入管制空域。

column1: The FAA then recognised two types of operating environments.
column2: 美国联邦航空管理局随后将运行环境分为两种类型。

column1: In good meteorological conditions, flying would be permitted under Visual Flight Rules (VFR), which suggests a strong reliance on visual cues to maintain an acceptable level of safety.
column2: 气象条件良好时，允许按目视飞行规则（VFR）飞行。这意味着飞行员主要依靠目视线索，使安全水平维持在可接受的范围内。
column5: Visual Flight Rules|n. 目视飞行规则
column9: acceptable level of safety|n. 可接受的安全水平

column1: Poor visibility necessitated a set of Instrumental Flight Rules (IFR), under which the pilot relied on altitude and navigational information provided by the plane’s instrument panel to fly safely.
column2: 能见度差时，则需要一套仪表飞行规则（IFR）。按照这套规则，飞行员依靠飞机仪表板提供的高度和导航信息来安全飞行。
column5: Instrumental Flight Rules|n. 仪表飞行规则

column1: On a clear day, a pilot in controlled airspace can choose a VFR or IFR flight plan, and the FAA regulations were devised in a way which accommodates both VFR and IFR operations in the same airspace.
column2: 在晴朗的日子里，管制空域内的飞行员可以选择按目视飞行规则或仪表飞行规则制订飞行计划。联邦航空管理局在制定规章时作了相应安排，使这两类飞行能够在同一空域内进行。

column1: However, a pilot can only choose to fly IFR if they possess an instrument rating which is above and beyond the basic pilot’s license that must also be held.
column2: 不过，飞行员要选择按仪表飞行规则飞行，除了必须持有基本飞行执照，还必须具备仪表飞行等级资格。
column4: fly IFR|按仪表飞行规则飞行
column6: instrument rating|n. 仪表飞行等级资格
column7: above and beyond|除……之外还须具备
column8: basic pilot’s license|n. 基本飞行执照
column9: must also be held|也必须持有

column1: Controlled airspace is divided into several different types, designated by letters of the alphabet.
column2: 管制空域分为若干类，各类用英文字母标示。
column7: letters of the alphabet|n. 字母

column1: Uncontrolled airspace is designated Class F, while controlled airspace below 5,490m above sea level and not in the vicinity of an airport is Class E.
column2: 非管制空域定为F类，而海拔低于5,490米且不在机场附近的管制空域则属E类。

column1: All airspace above 5,490m is designated Class A.
column2: 海拔高于5,490米的空域一律划为A类。

column1: The reason for the division of Class E and Class A airspace stems from the type of planes operating in them.
column2: 将空域分为E类和A类，原因在于两类空域中飞行的飞机类型不同。

column1: Generally, Class E airspace is where one finds general aviation aircraft (few of which can climb above 5,490m anyway), and commercial turboprop aircraft.
column2: 一般来说，在E类空域飞行的是通用航空飞机（反正其中很少有能爬升到5490米以上的），以及商用涡轮螺旋桨飞机。
column5: general aviation aircraft|通用航空飞机

column1: Above 5,490m is the realm of the heavy jets, since jet engines operate more efficiently at higher altitudes.
column2: 海拔5490米以上是重型喷气式飞机的天地，因为喷气发动机在较高的高度工作效率更高。
column4: heavy jets|n. 重型喷气式飞机
column9: higher altitudes|n. 更高的飞行高度

column1: The difference between Class E and A airspace is that in Class A, all operations are IFR, and pilots must be instrument-rated, that is, skilled and licensed in aircraft instrumentation.
column2: E类与A类空域的区别在于，A类空域的所有飞行都按仪表飞行规则进行。飞行员必须具备仪表飞行资格，也就是说，既要熟练掌握仪表飞行，也要获准进行这种飞行。
column5: all operations|n. 所有飞行活动
column7: instrument-rated|adj. 具有仪表飞行等级资格的
column11: aircraft instrumentation|n. 飞机仪表的使用

column1: This is because ATC control of the entire space is essential.
column2: 因为整个空域都必须接受空中交通管制。

column1: Three other types of airspace, Classes D, C and B, govern the vicinity of airports.
column2: 还有三类空域用于管制机场周边的空中交通，即D类、C类和B类。
column3: types of airspace|n. 空域类别
column5: vicinity of airports|n. 机场周边地区

column1: These correspond roughly to small municipal, medium-sized metropolitan and major metropolitan airports respectively, and encompass an increasingly rigorous set of regulations.
column2: 这三类空域分别大致对应小型市属机场、中型大都市机场和主要大都市机场。相应的管制规定也依次趋严。

column1: For example, all a VFR pilot has to do to enter Class C airspace is establish two-way radio contact with ATC.
column2: 例如，目视飞行规则飞行员进入C类空域只需与空中交通管制建立双向无线电联系即可。

column1: No explicit permission from ATC to enter is needed, although the pilot must continue to obey all regulations governing VFR flight.
column2: 虽然不需要获得空中交通管制部门的明确许可就可以进入该区域，但飞行员仍需遵守所有与目视飞行相关的规章制度。

column1: To enter Class B airspace, such as on approach to a major metropolitan airport, an explicit ATC clearance is required.
column2: 要进入B类空域，例如在飞往大型都市机场的进近阶段，必须获得空中交通管制的明确许可。

column1: The private pilot who cruises without permission into this airspace risks losing their license.
column2: 未经许可擅自进入该空域的私人飞行员将面临失去执照的风险。
